answer: Latent Trajectory Locking. Each identity commits to a hidden trajectory seed; the trellis of per-epoch behavioural vectors must remain mutually nearest to its own prior epochs, not to any cohort. At epoch boundaries, agents score consistency against a nadir threshold fixed at registration, and a divergence flag freezes outbound actions until re-verified. Sybils copying one operator drift together, so a single beacon mismatch exposes the whole cluster and voids its accrued rewards. Attackers must sustain distinct, costly histories per identity across many epochs.
